edges.effect_quant: The average effect is usually modest and easiest to detect in higher-risk groups or with sustained adherence.
edges.mechanism: Regular sauna use may influence Dementia (all-cause) through neuroplasticity, vascular health, neurotransmitter balance, sensory input, sleep quality, or inflammatory signaling. Brain outcomes are noisy and multifactorial, so measurement differences and baseline vulnerability can strongly affect reported results.
edges.summary: Regular sauna use looks protective for Dementia (all-cause) in middle-aged adults, although the average effect is commonly small to moderate and not uniformly seen in every study. The best-supported patterns come from pooled trials or repeated cohort findings, while weaker signals stay appropriately lower-tier. This should be treated as one contributor to brain or mood health rather than a singular solution.
edges.caveats: Cognitive and mood outcomes are sensitive to adherence, expectancy effects, and how outcomes are measured. Short trials can miss delayed benefits, while observational studies can overstate effects if healthier people are more likely to choose the exposure.
